1881.subject: Physics
1881.text: A block of mass $10 \mathrm{~kg}$ is moving in $x$-direction with a constant speed of $10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{sec}$. It is subjected to a retarding force $F=-0.1 x$ joule/m eter during its travel from $x=20$ meter to $x=30$ meter. Its final kinetic energy will be
1881.sol:
According to work energy theorem,

$\begin{aligned}$& W=$\Delta \mathrm{K} \cdot \mathrm{E} . \quad \Rightarrow$W=$\frac{1}{2}$m v_2^2-$\frac{1}{2}$m v_1^2 \\
\Rightarrow & F $\cdot$d x=$\mathrm{K} \cdot \mathrm{E} \cdot$f-$\frac{1}{2} \times$10 $\times$100 \\
\Rightarrow & F $\cdot$d x=$\mathrm{K} \cdot \mathrm{E} \cdot$f-500 \\
\Rightarrow & \int_{20}^{30}-0.1 x d x=$\mathrm{K} \cdot \mathrm{E} \cdot$f-500 \\
\Rightarrow & -0.1$\left[\frac{x^2}{2}\right]_{20}^{30}=\mathrm{K} \cdot \mathrm{E} \cdot$f-500 \\
\Rightarrow & -0.1$\left[\frac{900-400}{2}\right]=\mathrm{K} \cdot \mathrm{E} \cdot$f-500
\end{aligned}

\Rightarrow $\mathrm{K}_{\cdot} \mathrm{E}_{\cdot f}=$500-25=475 $\mathrm{~J}$

2188.subject: Zoology
2188.text:
Assertion : Astigmatism is due to uneven curvature of lens.
Reason : It is treated with cylindrical lenses.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
2188.sol: Astigmatism is a defect of vision in which the image of an object is distorted, usually in either the vertical or the horizontal axis, because not all the light rays come of a focus on the retina. Some parts of the object may be in focus but light from other parts may be focused in front of or behind the retina. This is usually due to abnormal curvature of the cornea and/ or lens whose surface resembles part of sphere. The defect can be corrected by wearing cylindrical lenses, called toric contact lens which produce exactly the opposite degree of distortion and thus cancel out the distortion caused by the eye itself.
2188.meta: Assertion : Astigmatism is due to uneven curvature of lens. Reason : It is treated with cylindrical lenses.

$\dfrac{x}{m} = k \cdot p^{1 / n}\left(n > 1\right) ⇒ log\dfrac{x}{m} = logk + \dfrac{1}{n}logP$

Since adsorption is an exothermic process, it decreases with increase in temperature and varies inversely proportional to temperature.

$\dfrac{x}{m} ∝ \dfrac{1}{T}$

So, according to the given graph, $\dfrac{x}{m}$ is more for& ${T}_{3}$. So, ${T}_{3}$ is the least temperature and& the correct order is& ${T}_{3} < {T}_{2} < {T}_{1}$.

According to the Bohr's model,
\(m v r=\frac{n h}{2 \pi} \Rightarrow m r^2 \omega=\frac{n h}{2 \pi} \quad \ldots \text{ (iii) }\left[\because \omega=\frac{v}{r}\right]\)
(iii) \(\left[\because \omega=\frac{v}{r}\right]\)

1+4+9 & +\ldots n²=\Sigma n² \\
& =$\frac{n(n+1)(2 n+1)}{6}$\\
1+2+3+ & \ldots n=\Sigma n=$\frac{n(n+1)}{2}$\\
\therefore \quad x_{c m} & =$\frac{\ln (n+1)(2 n+1)}{6}=\frac{l(2 n+1)}{3}
\end{aligned}$

& =$\left[\frac{8.64 \times 10^4 \times 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \times 5.98 \times 10^{24}}{4 \times(3.14)^2}\right]^{1 / 3}-$6.4 $\times$10^6 \\
& =42.25 $\times$10^6-6.4 $\times$10^6=35.85 $\times$10^6 $\mathrm{~m}$\\

\end{aligned}$

Now, any point on the line $l$ is given by

The direction ratios of $AP$ are

And the direction ratios of $l$ are$- 2, 6$ and $- 3$.

Given, $AP ⊥ l$

$⇒ \lambda = \dfrac{13}{49}$

$= 22 - 26\lambda + 49{λ}^{2}$

19862.subject: Chemistry
19862.text: The initial amount of 2 radioactive elements X and Y is 1 g each and their half-lives are 12 hours and 16 hours respectively. The ratio of X and Y after 2 days is:
19862.sol:
The amount of a radioactive substance remaining after time $t$ is given by $N(t) = N_0 \left( \dfrac{1}{2} \right)^{t/T_{1/2}}$, where $N_0$ is the initial amount and $T_{1/2}$ is the half-life.

Given $t = 2$ days = $48$ hours.

For element X: $N_0 = 1$ g, $T_{1/2} = 12$ hours. The number of half-lives is $n_X = \dfrac{48}{12} = 4$.

$N_X = 1 \times \left( \dfrac{1}{2} \right)^{4} = \dfrac{1}{16}$ g.

For element Y: $N_0 = 1$ g, $T_{1/2} = 16$ hours. The number of half-lives is $n_Y = \dfrac{48}{16} = 3$.

$N_Y = 1 \times \left( \dfrac{1}{2} \right)^{3} = \dfrac{1}{8}$ g.

The ratio of X to Y after 2 days is $\dfrac{N_X}{N_Y} = \dfrac{1/16}{1/8} = \dfrac{8}{16} = \dfrac{1}{2}$.

Answer: 1:2

20152.subject: Chemistry
20152.text:
The $\mathrm{E}^{{}^{\circ}}$ values of $\mathrm{A}. \mathrm{B}$ and $\mathrm{C}$ are given. Which element/(s) is/(are) good for coating the surface of iron to prevent corrosion?
Given: $[\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{Fe}^{2+} / \mathrm{Fe}^0=-0.44 \mathrm{ V} ; \quad \mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{A}^{2+} / \mathrm{A}^0=-2.37 \mathrm{ V} ; \quad \mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{B}^{2+} / \mathrm{B}^0=-0.15 \mathrm{ V} ; \quad \mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{C}^{2+} / \mathrm{C}^0=+0.34 \mathrm{ V}]$
20152.sol:
To prevent the corrosion of iron, the metal used for coating must act as a sacrificial anode. This means the coating metal must have a more negative standard reduction potential than that of iron ($E^{{}^{\circ}}_{Fe^{2+}/Fe} = -0.44 \text{ V}$).

Comparing the given standard reduction potentials:
$E^{{}^{\circ}}_{A^{2+}/A} = -2.37 \text{ V}$
$E^{{}^{\circ}}_{B^{2+}/B} = -0.15 \text{ V}$
$E^{{}^{\circ}}_{C^{2+}/C} = +0.34 \text{ V}$

Since $-2.37 \text{ V} < -0.44 \text{ V}$, element A has a lower reduction potential than iron. Therefore, element A can act as a sacrificial anode and protect iron from corrosion.

Elements B and C have reduction potentials greater than $-0.44 \text{ V}$, meaning they are more noble than iron and would not provide sacrificial protection.

Answer: Element A only

20414.subject: Chemistry
20414.text:
From among the following, identify the compound which forms two moles of a ketone on ozonolysis.
[A] 2,3-Dimethylbutane.
[B] 3-Methyl-1-pentene.
[C] 2,3-Dimethyl-2-butene.
[D] 2-Methyl-2-pentane.
20414.sol:
Ozonolysis of an alkene involves the cleavage of the carbon-carbon double bond to form carbonyl compounds. The general reaction is $R_1R_2C=CR_3R_4 \xrightarrow{O_3, Zn/H_2O} R_1R_2C=O + R_3R_4C=O$.

For the product to be two moles of a ketone, the alkene must be symmetric and substituted such that each carbon of the double bond is attached to two alkyl groups.

Analyzing the options:
[A] 2,3-Dimethylbutane is an alkane and does not undergo ozonolysis.
[B] 3-Methyl-1-pentene is $CH_2=CH-CH(CH_3)CH_2CH_3$. Ozonolysis yields formaldehyde ($HCHO$) and 2-methylbutanal.
[C] 2,3-Dimethyl-2-butene is $(CH_3)_2C=C(CH_3)_2$. Ozonolysis yields two moles of acetone ($CH_3COCH_3$), which is a ketone.
[D] 2-Methyl-2-pentene (assuming the intended structure) is $(CH_3)_2C=CH-CH_2CH_3$. Ozonolysis yields acetone and propanal.

Answer: [C]

20929.subject: Mathematics
20929.text: A man is moving away from a tower 41.6 m high at a rate of $2 \mathrm{ m} / \mathrm{s}$. If the eyelevel of the man is 1.6 m above the ground, then the rate at which the angle of elevation of the top of the tower changes, when he is at a distance of 30 m from the foot of the tower is
20929.sol:
Let $h$ be the height of the tower, $h = 41.6$ m. Let $h_0$ be the height of the man's eye level, $h_0 = 1.6$ m. The effective height of the tower above the man's eye level is $H = h - h_0 = 41.6 - 1.6 = 40$ m.

Let $x$ be the distance of the man from the foot of the tower. The angle of elevation $\theta$ is given by $\tan \theta = \dfrac{H}{x} = \dfrac{40}{x}$.

Differentiating both sides with respect to time $t$, we get $\sec^2 \theta \cdot \dfrac{d\theta}{dt} = -\dfrac{40}{x^2} \cdot \dfrac{dx}{dt}$.

Given $\dfrac{dx}{dt} = 2$ m/s and $x = 30$ m. At $x = 30$, $\tan \theta = \dfrac{40}{30} = \dfrac{4}{3}$.

Since $\tan \theta = \dfrac{4}{3}$, we have $\sec^2 \theta = 1 + \tan^2 \theta = 1 + \left(\dfrac{4}{3}\right)^2 = 1 + \dfrac{16}{9} = \dfrac{25}{9}$.

Substituting the values into the differentiated equation: $\dfrac{25}{9} \cdot \dfrac{d\theta}{dt} = -\dfrac{40}{30^2} \cdot 2$.

$\dfrac{25}{9} \cdot \dfrac{d\theta}{dt} = -\dfrac{40}{900} \cdot 2 = -\dfrac{80}{900} = -\dfrac{8}{90} = -\dfrac{4}{45}$.

$\dfrac{d\theta}{dt} = -\dfrac{4}{45} \cdot \dfrac{9}{25} = -\dfrac{4}{5 \cdot 5} = -\dfrac{4}{125}$ rad/s.

Answer: $-\dfrac{4}{125} \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm\sec$

Calculate the distance that will separate the two balls when they hit the ground.
23237.sol:
The time taken for a ball thrown horizontally from a height $h$ to reach the ground is given by $t = \sqrt{\dfrac{2h}{g}}$.

For the first ball thrown from height $h_1 = 3$ m:
$t_1 = \sqrt{\dfrac{2 \times 3}{9.8}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{6}{9.8}} \approx 0.7825$ s.

The horizontal distance covered by the first ball is $x_1 = v \times t_1 = 6 \times 0.7825 = 4.695$ m.

For the second ball thrown from height $h_2 = 6$ m:
$t_2 = \sqrt{\dfrac{2 \times 6}{9.8}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{12}{9.8}} \approx 1.1066$ s.

The horizontal distance covered by the second ball is $x_2 = v \times t_2 = 6 \times 1.1066 = 6.6396$ m.

The distance separating the two balls when they hit the ground is the difference in their horizontal ranges:
$\Delta x = x_2 - x_1 = 6.6396 - 4.695 = 1.9446$ m.

Rounding to two decimal places, the distance is $1.94$ m.

Answer: 1.94 m

23649.subject: Physics
23649.text: In Young's double slit experiment the ratio of phase difference between light waves reaching the third bright fringe and third dark fringe is
23649.sol:
In Young's double slit experiment, the path difference $\Delta x$ for the $n$-th bright fringe is given by $\Delta x = n\lambda$, where $n = 0, 1, 2, \dots$.

The phase difference $\phi$ is related to the path difference by $\phi = \dfrac{2\pi}{\lambda} \Delta x$.

For the third bright fringe, $n = 3$. Thus, the path difference is $\Delta x_{bright} = 3\lambda$.

The phase difference for the third bright fringe is $\phi_{bright} = \dfrac{2\pi}{\lambda} \times 3\lambda = 6\pi$.

The path difference for the $n$-th dark fringe is given by $\Delta x = (2n - 1)\dfrac{\lambda}{2}$, where $n = 1, 2, 3, \dots$.

For the third dark fringe, $n = 3$. Thus, the path difference is $\Delta x_{dark} = (2 \times 3 - 1)\dfrac{\lambda}{2} = \dfrac{5\lambda}{2}$.

The phase difference for the third dark fringe is $\phi_{dark} = \dfrac{2\pi}{\lambda} \times \dfrac{5\lambda}{2} = 5\pi$.

The ratio of the phase difference of the third bright fringe to the third dark fringe is $\dfrac{\phi_{bright}}{\phi_{dark}} = \dfrac{6\pi}{5\pi} = \dfrac{6}{5}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{6}{5}$

26318.subject: Physics
26318.text: Which one of the following options represents the magnetic field $\overset{\to}{B}$ at $O$ due to the current flowing in the given wire segments lying on the $xy$ plane?
26318.sol:
Magnetic field due to a straight wire will be zero if the line of the wire passes through the point of interest. Therefore, In the above figure,

${B}_{BC} + {B}_{DE} + {B}_{FG} = 0$

Therefore,

$\overset{\to}{B}net = \overset{\to}{B}AB + \overset{\to}{B}CD + \overset{\to}{B}EF$

Magnetic field due to a finite wire is given by,

$B = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}I}{4\pid}\left(sin\alpha + sin\beta\right)$

Using above formula,

$\overset{\to}{B}AB = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}I}{4\piL} \times \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\left(- \overset{^}{k}\right)$

Magnetic field due to a circular arc is,

$B = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}I}{2R} \times \dfrac{\theta}{2\pi}$

Therefore,

$\overset{\to}{B}CD = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}I}{4\left(\dfrac{L}{2}\right)}\left(- \overset{^}{k}\right)$ and $\overset{\to}{B}EF = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}I}{8 \times \left(\dfrac{L}{4}\right)}\left(- \overset{^}{k}\right)$

Therefore, net magnetic field

$\overset{\to}{B}net = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}I}{4\pi \times L}\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right) + \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}I}{4\left(\dfrac{L}{2}\right)} + \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}I}{8 \times \left(\dfrac{L}{4}\right)}\left(- \overset{^}{k}\right)$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{B}net = \left(\dfrac{{\mu}_{0}I}{2L} + \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}I}{2L} + \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}I}{4\sqrt{2}\piL}\right)\left(- \overset{^}{k}\right)$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{B}net = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}I}{L}\left(1 + \dfrac{1}{4\sqrt{2}\pi}\right)\left(- \overset{^}{k}\right)$

26424.subject: Physics
26424.text: A particle is thrown with a speed $v$ from a point $O$ at an angle $\theta$ with the horizontal plane such that it passes through the point $P$ at a height of $1$ m and horizontal distance of $5$ m from $O$, as shown in the figure. If acceleration due to gravity is $g$ ms$^{-2}$, then the correct statement(s) is/are:
options: If $\theta = 45^\circ$, the particle reaches its maximum height before it reaches $P$.
If $\theta = 30^\circ$, the particle reaches its maximum height after reaching $P$.
26424.sol:
The equation of trajectory of a projectile is given by:

$y = x \tan \theta - \dfrac{g x^2}{2 v^2 \cos^2 \theta}$

The particle passes through point $P(5, 1)$. Substituting $x = 5$ and $y = 1$:

$1 = 5 \tan \theta - \dfrac{25 g}{2 v^2 \cos^2 \theta}$

For option (A), substituting $\theta = 45^\circ$:

$1 = 5 \tan 45^\circ - \dfrac{25 g}{2 v^2 \cos^2 45^\circ}$

$1 = 5(1) - \dfrac{25 g}{2 v^2 (1/2)}$

$1 = 5 - \dfrac{25 g}{v^2}$

$\dfrac{25 g}{v^2} = 4 \Rightarrow v^2 = \dfrac{25 g}{4} \Rightarrow v = \dfrac{5\sqrt{g}}{2}$ ms$^{-1}$

Thus, option (A) is correct.

For option (B), the horizontal distance to the maximum height is $x_m = \dfrac{R}{2} = \dfrac{v^2 \sin(2\theta)}{2g}$.

For $\theta = 45^\circ$ and $v^2 = \dfrac{25g}{4}$:

$x_m = \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{25g}{4}\right) \sin 90^\circ}{2g} = \dfrac{25}{8} = 3.125$ m

Since $x_m = 3.125$ m $< 5$ m, the particle reaches its maximum height before it reaches $P$. Thus, option (B) is correct.

For option (C), substituting $\theta = 30^\circ$ into the trajectory equation:

$1 = 5 \tan 30^\circ - \dfrac{25 g}{2 v^2 \cos^2 30^\circ}$

$1 = \dfrac{5}{\sqrt{3}} - \dfrac{25 g}{2 v^2 (3/4)} \Rightarrow \dfrac{50 g}{3 v^2} = \dfrac{5}{\sqrt{3}} - 1$

$v^2 = \dfrac{50\sqrt{3}g}{3(5 - \sqrt{3})}$

The horizontal distance to the maximum height is:

$x_m = \dfrac{v^2 \sin 60^\circ}{2g} = \dfrac{v^2 \sqrt{3}}{4g} = \dfrac{50\sqrt{3}g}{3(5 - \sqrt{3})} \times \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{4g} = \dfrac{25}{2(5 - \sqrt{3})} \approx 3.82$ m

Since $x_m < 5$ m, the particle reaches its maximum height before reaching $P$. Thus, option (C) is incorrect.

For option (D), substituting $\theta = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{5}\right)$, so $\tan \theta = \dfrac{1}{5}$:

$1 = 5\left(\dfrac{1}{5}\right) - \dfrac{25 g}{2 v^2 \cos^2 \theta} \Rightarrow 1 = 1 - \dfrac{25 g}{2 v^2 \cos^2 \theta}$

$\dfrac{25 g}{2 v^2 \cos^2 \theta} = 0$

This is only possible if $v \to \infty$. Thus, option (D) is incorrect.

Answer: If $\theta = 45^\circ$, then $v = \dfrac{5\sqrt{g}}{2}$ ms$^{-1}$.; If $\theta = 45^\circ$, the particle reaches its maximum height before it reaches $P$.

26812.subject: Chemistry
26812.text:
Consider the following sequence of reactions

The major product P is:
26812.sol:
Step 1: The first reagent is Cu at $573\text{ K}$. When a tertiary alcohol like tert-butyl alcohol is passed over heated copper at $573\text{ K}$, it undergoes dehydration rather than dehydrogenation to form an alkene.

$(CH_3)_3C-OH \xrightarrow{Cu / 573\text{ K}} CH_2=C(CH_3)_2 + H_2O$
The intermediate product is isobutylene (2-methylpropene).

Step 2: The second set of reagents is $H^+$ and $PhCOOH$ (benzoic acid). This is an acid-catalyzed addition of a carboxylic acid to an alkene, which is a standard method for synthesizing tert-butyl esters.
First, the alkene is protonated by the acid to form the most stable carbocation, which is the tertiary butyl carbocation:
$CH_2=C(CH_3)_2 + H^+ \rightleftharpoons (CH_3)_3C^+$

Next, the carboxylic acid acts as a nucleophile and attacks the carbocation. The oxygen atom of the benzoic acid attacks the tert-butyl carbocation, followed by deprotonation:
$PhCOOH + (CH_3)_3C^+ \rightleftharpoons Ph-CO-O^+(H)-C(CH_3)_3 \rightleftharpoons Ph-CO-O-C(CH_3)_3 + H^+$

The final major product is tert-butyl benzoate. Electrophilic aromatic substitution (Friedel-Crafts alkylation) on the benzene ring does not occur here because the $-COOH$ group is strongly deactivating, making O-alkylation (ester formation) the highly preferred pathway.

Comparing this with the given options, Option (C) represents the structure of tert-butyl benzoate.

Answer:

29805.text: The number of possible isomeric products formed when $3$-chloro-$1$-butene reacts with $HCl$ through carbocation formation is.........
29805.sol:
3-chloro-1-butene undergo protonation and gives secondary carbocation according Markonikov's addition in the first step. 30200.subject: Chemistry
30200.text: $RMgI$ when treated with ice cold water liberated a gas which occupied $1.4\text{ dm}^3/\text{g}$ at STP. The gas produced is further reacted with iodine in presence of $HIO_3$ to give compound (X). Compound (X) in presence of Na and dry ether produced compound (Y). Molar mass of compound (Y) is _______ $\text{g mol}^{-1}$. (Nearest integer)
30200.sol:
The reaction of Grignard reagent with water yields an alkane:

$RMgI + H_2O \rightarrow RH + Mg(OH)I$

Given that $1 \text{ g}$ of the gas $RH$ occupies $1.4 \text{ dm}^3$ at STP, we can find its molar mass. Using the standard molar volume at STP ($22.4 \text{ dm}^3$):

$\text{Molar mass of } RH = \dfrac{22.4 \text{ dm}^3 \text{ mol}^{-1}}{1.4 \text{ dm}^3 \text{ g}^{-1}} = 16 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$

The alkane with a molar mass of $16 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$ is methane ($CH_4$).

Methane reacts with iodine in the presence of an oxidizing agent like $HIO_3$ (which prevents the backward reaction by consuming the formed $HI$) to give methyl iodide:

$CH_4 + I_2 \xrightarrow{HIO_3} CH_3I + HI$

Thus, compound (X) is methyl iodide ($CH_3I$).

Compound (X) undergoes the Wurtz reaction when treated with sodium and dry ether to form a higher alkane:

$2CH_3I + 2Na \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} CH_3-CH_3 + 2NaI$

Compound (Y) is ethane ($C_2H_6$).

The molar mass of ethane ($C_2H_6$) is:

$2 \times 12 + 6 \times 1 = 30 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$

Answer: $30$

31559.subject: Chemistry
31559.text: The incorrect statement about the imperfections in solids is
options: Schottky defect decreases the density of the substance.
Frenkel defect does not alter the density of the substance.
Interstitial defect increases the density of the substance.
Vacancy defect increases the density of the substance.
31559.sol:
Frenkel Defect: This defect is shown by ionic solids. The smaller ion (usually cation) is dislocated from its normal site to an interstitial site. It creates a vacancy defect at its original site and an interstitial defect at its new location. Frenkel defect is also called dislocation defect. It does not change the density of the solid. In all other defects there is a change in the density.

In Schottky defect equal number of cation and anion are missing from their position so, it decreases the density of the substance.

In Interstitial defect extra atoms are present at interstitial position so, it increases the density of the substance.

Due to vacancy defect density of the substance will decrease. since atoms are missing from their positions.

38323.text: Let $S = \left[- \pi, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) - \left\{- \dfrac{\pi}{2}, - \dfrac{\pi}{4}, - \dfrac{3\pi}{4}, \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right\}$. Then the number of elements in the set $A = \left\{\theta \in S: tan\theta\left(1 + \sqrt{5}tan\left(2\theta\right)\right) = \sqrt{5} - tan\left(2\theta\right)\right\}$ is _____ .
38323.sol:
Given,

$S = \left[- \pi, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) - \left\{- \dfrac{\pi}{2}, - \dfrac{\pi}{4}, - \dfrac{3\pi}{4}, \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right\}$ and the set $A = \left\{\theta \in S: tan\theta\left(1 + \sqrt{5}tan\left(2\theta\right)\right) = \sqrt{5} - tan\left(2\theta\right)\right\}$

Now let $tan\alpha = \sqrt{5}$

So, $tan\theta\left(1 + \sqrt{5}tan\left(2\theta\right)\right) = \sqrt{5} - tan\left(2\theta\right)$ becomes,

$⇒ tan\theta\left(1 + tan\alphatan\left(2\theta\right)\right) = tan\alpha - tan\left(2\theta\right)$

On rearranging we get,

$⇒ tan\theta = \dfrac{tan\alpha - tan2\theta}{1 + tan\alphatan2\theta}$

On using formula $tan\left(A - B\right) = \dfrac{tanA - tanB}{1 - tanAtanB}$ we get,

$⇒ tan\theta = tan\left(\alpha - 2\theta\right)$

$⇒ \alpha - 2\theta = n\pi + \theta$

$⇒ 3\theta = \alpha - n\pi$

$⇒ \theta = \dfrac{\alpha}{3} - \dfrac{n\pi}{3}; n \in Z$

If $\theta \in [ - \pi, \pi / 2 )$ then $n = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4$ are acceptable solution

So, total $5$ solutions are possible.

38374.sol:
Starting with $\frac{\tan(A-B)}{\tan A} + \frac{\sin^2 C}{\sin^2 A} = 1$, rearrange to $\frac{\tan(A-B)}{\tan A} = 1 - \frac{\sin^2 C}{\sin^2 A}$.
$\Rightarrow \tan(A-B) \tan A = \sin^2 A - \sin^2 C$.
Applying the identity $\sin^2 \theta = \frac{\tan^2 \theta}{1+\tan^2 \theta}$ and simplifying leads to a relationship between the tangent values.
The constraint reduces to $(\tan C)^2 = \tan A \cdot \tan B$, which means $\tan A$, $\tan C$, and $\tan B$ form a geometric progression with common ratio $r = \frac{\tan C}{\tan A}$.

38396.sol:
Let $\theta + \left(m - 1\right)\dfrac{\pi}{6} = x$ and $\theta + m\dfrac{\pi}{6} = y$

So, $y - x = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$

Now, $\mathop{∑}_{m = 1}^{9}sec\left(\theta + \left(m - 1\right)\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)sec\left(\theta + \dfrac{m\pi}{6}\right)$

$= \mathop{∑}_{m = 1}^{9}secxsecy = \mathop{∑}_{m = 1}^{9}\dfrac{1}{cosxcosy}$

$= 2\mathop{∑}_{m = 1}^{9}\dfrac{sin\left(y - x\right)}{cosxcosy} = 2\mathop{∑}_{m = 1}^{9}\left(tany - tanx\right)$

$= 2\mathop{∑}_{m = 1}^{9}\left(tan\left(\theta + m\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right) - tan\left(\theta + ( m - 1 ) \dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)\right)$

$= 2\left(tan\left(\theta + \dfrac{\pi}{6}\right) - tan\left(\theta + \dfrac{0 \cdot \pi}{6}\right)\right) + 2\left(tan\left(\theta + 2\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right) - tan\left(\theta + \dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)\right)$

$+ 2\left(tan\left(\theta + 3\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right) - tan\left(\theta + 2\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)\right) + . . . + 2\left(tan\left(\theta + 9\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right) - tan\left(\theta + 8\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)\right)$

$= 2\left(tan\left(\theta + \dfrac{9\pi}{6}\right) - tan\theta\right) = 2\left(- cot\theta - tan\theta\right)$

i.e. $2\left(- cot\theta - tan\theta\right) = - \dfrac{8}{\sqrt{3}}$ (Given)

$∴ tan\theta + cot\theta = \dfrac{4}{\sqrt{3}}$

$⇒ tan\theta = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$ or $\sqrt{3}$ (as $\theta \in \left(0, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$)

So, $S = \left\{\dfrac{\pi}{6}, \dfrac{\pi}{3}\right\}$

Hence, $\mathop{∑}_{\theta \in S}\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{6} + \dfrac{\pi}{3} = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$

38449.subject: Mathematics
38449.text: Let $P Q R$ be a triangle such that $\overrightarrow{P Q}=-2 \hat{i}-\hat{j}+2 \hat{k}$ and $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{PR}}=a \hat{\mathrm{i}}+b \hat{\mathrm{j}}-4 \hat{\mathrm{k}}, a, b \in \mathbb{Z}$. Let S be the point on QR, which is equidistant from the lines PQ and PR. If $|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{PR}}|=9$ and $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{PS}}=\hat{\mathrm{i}}-7 \hat{\mathrm{j}}+2 \hat{\mathrm{k}}$, then the value of $3 a-4 b$ is $\_\_\_\_$
38449.sol:
Given: $\vec{PQ} = -2\hat{i} - \hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$, $\vec{PR} = a\hat{i} + b\hat{j} - 4\hat{k}$ ($a, b \in \mathbb{Z}$), $\vec{PS} = \hat{i} - 7\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$, $|\vec{PR}| = 9$
From $|\vec{PR}| = 9$: $a^2 + b^2 + 16 = 81 \Rightarrow a^2 + b^2 = 65$ ...(1)
Since S is on QR equidistant from lines PQ and PR, PS is the angle bisector. So:
$\cos\theta = \frac{\vec{PQ} \cdot \vec{PS}}{|\vec{PQ}||\vec{PS}|} = \frac{-2+7+4}{3 \cdot 3\sqrt{6}} = \frac{9}{9\sqrt{6}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}$
Similarly: $\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}} = \frac{\vec{PS} \cdot \vec{PR}}{|\vec{PS}||\vec{PR}|} = \frac{a - 7b - 8}{3\sqrt{6} \cdot 9}$
$a - 7b = 35$ ...(2)
From (1) and (2): $a = 7, b = -4$
$3a - 4b = 21 + 16 = 37$ (NTA Answer)
However, $\vec{QS} = 3\hat{i} - 6\hat{j}$ and $\vec{SR} = 6\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} - 6\hat{k}$ are not parallel, so Q, S, R are not collinear. Also $\cos\theta = \frac{2\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{3}} > 1$, which is impossible. Hence no such triangle exists.
So, this should be a bonus question.

39975.text:
In photoelectric effect
A. The photocurrent is proportional to the intensity of the incident radiation.
B. Maximum kinetic energy with which photoelectrons are emitted depends on the intensity of incident light.
C. Max K.E. with which photoelectrons are emitted depends on the frequency of incident light.
D. The emission of photoelectrons require a minimum threshold intensity of incident radiation.
E. Max K.E. of the photoelectrons is independent of the frequency of the incident light.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
39975.sol:
With proper energetic radiation, the photoelectric current increases with an increase in accelerating potential until it reaches a point where it reaches its maximum and does not increase with an additional increase in accelerating potential.

For a given potential difference, the photocurrent is directly proportional to the intensity of the incident radiation.

The maximum kinetic energy of the emitted photoelectrons can be written as

${K}_{max} = hν - \phi$

From above equation, it can be seen that the maximum kinetic energy of the photoelectron depends on the frequency of the light used.

Hence, the statements A and C are correct.

40807.subject: Physics
40807.text:
A body of mass $m$ is taken from the surface of earth to a height equal to twice the radius of earth ($R_e$). The increase in potential energy will be _______.
($g$ is acceleration due to gravity at the surface of earth)
40807.sol:
Initial potential energy of the body at the surface of the earth is given by:

$U_i = -\dfrac{GMm}{R_e}$

Final potential energy of the body at a height $h = 2R_e$ from the surface of the earth is:

$U_f = -\dfrac{GMm}{R_e + h} = -\dfrac{GMm}{R_e + 2R_e} = -\dfrac{GMm}{3R_e}$

The increase in potential energy is:

$\Delta U = U_f - U_i = -\dfrac{GMm}{3R_e} - \left(-\dfrac{GMm}{R_e}\right)$

$\Delta U = \dfrac{GMm}{R_e} \left(1 - \dfrac{1}{3}\right) = \dfrac{2GMm}{3R_e}$

Acceleration due to gravity at the surface of the earth is $g = \dfrac{GM}{R_e^2}$, which gives $GM = gR_e^2$.

Substituting this value, we get:

$\Delta U = \dfrac{2(gR_e^2)m}{3R_e} = \dfrac{2}{3}mgR_e$

Answer: $\dfrac{2}{3}mgR_e$

Then, ${W}^{'} = m{g}^{'} = \dfrac{mg}{100} = \dfrac{W}{100}$

41525.subject: Physics
41525.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement $I$: The electric force changes the speed of the charged particle and hence changes its kinetic energy; whereas the magnetic force does not change the kinetic energy of the charged particle.
Statement $II$: The electric force accelerates the positively charged particle perpendicular to the direction of electric field. The magnetic force accelerates the moving charged particle along the direction of magnetic field.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement $I$ and Statement $II$ are correct.
Both Statement $I$ and Statement $II$ are incorrect.
Statement $I$ is correct but Statement $II$ is incorrect.
Statement $I$ is incorrect but Statement $II$ is correct.
41525.sol:
When a charged particle moves in an electric field, the field applies an electric force $\left(\overset{\to}{F} = q\overset{\to}{E}\right)$ along the field, so work done by electric field is non-zero resulting in accelerated motion, thus kinetic energy changes.

When a particle moves in a uniform magnetic field, the force due to magnetic field on it is perpendicular to its velocity, as force $\left(\overset{\to}{F} = q\overset{\to}{v} \times \overset{\to}{B}\right)$.
Since the magnetic field is constant, so force is constant. So, its direction of velocity constantly changes, but magnitude of velocity remains same. Hence, kinetic energy also does not change.

Electric field accelerates the particle in the direction of field $\left(\overset{\to}{F} = q\overset{\to}{E} = m\overset{\to}{a}\right)$and magnetic field accelerates the particle perpendicular to the field $\left(\overset{\to}{F} = q\overset{\to}{v} \times \overset{\to}{B} = m\overset{\to}{a}\right)$.

$W = 1.92\pi \times 10^{-4}$ J

42075.text:
Two wires as shown in the figure below, made of steel and have breaking stress of $12 \times 10^8$ N/m$^2$. Area of cross-section of upper wire is $0.008$ cm$^2$ and of lower wire is $0.004$ cm$^2$. The maximum mass that can be added to pan without breaking any wire is _____ kg.
(take $g = 10$ m/s$^2$)
42075.sol:
Let the maximum mass that can be added to the pan be $m$.

The breaking stress for both wires is $\sigma_{max} = 12 \times 10^8 \text{ N/m}^2$.

For the upper wire:
Area of cross-section, $A_u = 0.008 \text{ cm}^2 = 8 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}^2$
Maximum tension the upper wire can withstand is:
$T_{u,max} = \sigma_{max} \times A_u = (12 \times 10^8) \times (8 \times 10^{-7}) = 960 \text{ N}$
The total mass supported by the upper wire is $(30 + 10 + m) = (40 + m) \text{ kg}$.
Tension in the upper wire, $T_u = (40 + m)g = (40 + m) \times 10$
To avoid breaking the upper wire:
$(40 + m) \times 10 \le 960$
$40 + m \le 96 \implies m \le 56 \text{ kg}$

For the lower wire:
Area of cross-section, $A_l = 0.004 \text{ cm}^2 = 4 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}^2$
Maximum tension the lower wire can withstand is:
$T_{l,max} = \sigma_{max} \times A_l = (12 \times 10^8) \times (4 \times 10^{-7}) = 480 \text{ N}$
The total mass supported by the lower wire is $(10 + m) \text{ kg}$.
Tension in the lower wire, $T_l = (10 + m)g = (10 + m) \times 10$
To avoid breaking the lower wire:
$(10 + m) \times 10 \le 480$
$10 + m \le 48 \implies m \le 38 \text{ kg}$

To ensure neither wire breaks, the added mass $m$ must satisfy both conditions. Therefore, the maximum mass that can be added is the smaller of the two values:
$m = 38 \text{ kg}$

Answer: $38$

42082.text: Two wires $A$ and $B$ made of different materials of lengths 6.0 cm and 5.4 cm, respectively and area of cross sections $3.0 \times 10^{-5} \mathrm{~m}^{2}$ and $4.5 \times 10^{-5} \mathrm{~m}^{2}$, respectively are stretched by the same magnitude under a given load. The ratio of the Young's modulus of $A$ to that of $B$ is $x: 3$. The value of $x$ is $\_\_\_\_$.
42082.sol:
Young's modulus: $Y = \frac{\sigma}{\epsilon} = \frac{F/A}{\Delta L/L}$.
When the same force is applied and both wires stretch by the same extension $\Delta L$, the ratio of Young's moduli is:
$\frac{Y_A}{Y_B} = \frac{F/A_A}{\Delta L/L_A} \times \frac{\Delta L/L_B}{F/A_B} = \frac{A_B}{A_A} \times \frac{L_A}{L_B}$
$=\frac{4.5 \times 10^{-5}}{3.0 \times 10^{-5}} \times \frac{6.0}{5.4} = 1.5 \times \frac{10}{9} = \frac{5}{3}$.
Therefore $x : 3 = 5 : 3$, giving $x = 5$.

42171.sol: Shearing strain is created along the side surface of the punched disk. Note that the forces exerted on the disk are exerted along the circumference of the disk, and the total force exerted on its center only. Let us assume that the shearing stress along the side surface of the disk is uniform, then $\begin{aligned}\mathrm{F}>& \int_{\text{surface }} \mathrm{dF}_{\max }=\int_{\text{surface }} \sigma_{\max } \mathrm{dA}=\sigma_{\max } \int_{\text{surface }} \mathrm{dA}\\ &=\int \sigma_{\max } \cdot \mathrm{A}=\sigma_{\max } \cdot2 \pi\left(\frac{\mathrm{D}}{2}\right) \mathrm{h}\\ &=3.5 \times10^8 \times \ \left(\frac{1}{2} \times10^{-2}\right)\times0.3 \times10^{-2} \times2 \pi\\ &=3.297 \times10^4 \simeq 3.3 \times10^4 \mathrm{ N} \end{aligned}$

& \eta_{12}-\eta_1=\frac{200}{473}-\frac{100}{473}=\frac{100}{473} < \frac{100}{373} \\
\Rightarrow & \eta_{12}-\eta_1 < \eta_2 \\
\text{$ or $} & \eta_{12} < \eta_1+\eta_2
\end{aligned}$

44122.text:
Assertion A: Product of Pressure $\left(P\right)$ and time $\left(t\right)$ has the same dimension as that of coefficient of viscosity.

Reason: Coefficient of viscosity $= \dfrac{Force}{Velocitygradient}$
options: Both A and R true, and R is correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
44122.sol:
Viscous force is given by $F = ηA\left(\dfrac{d v}{d t}\right)$, here, $A$ is area and $\dfrac{d v}{d t}$ is velocity gradient.

Thus, $η = \dfrac{F}{A\left(\dfrac{d v}{d t}\right)}$.

Now, $Pt = \dfrac{F}{A}t = η\left(\dfrac{d v}{d t}\right)t$

Then, $\left[Pt\right] = M{L}^{- 1}{T}^{- 1} = \left[η\right]$

Thus, assertion is true but reason is false.

44333.text: A single slit of width $b$ is illuminated by a coherent monochromatic light of wavelength $\lambda .$ If the second and fourth minima in the diffraction pattern at a distance $1cm$ from the slit are at $3cm$ and $6cm$ respectively from the central maximum, what is the width of the central maximum? For secondary minima $dsin ⁡ \theta = n\lambda$

For second minima
$n = 2$
$sin ⁡ \theta = \dfrac{2\lambda}{d} = tan ⁡ {\theta}_{1} = \dfrac{{x}_{1}}{D}$
For fourth minima $n = 4$
${sin ⁡ \theta}_{2} = \dfrac{4\lambda}{d} = \dfrac{{x}_{2}}{D}$

Distance between both minima is ${x}_{2} - {x}_{1} = \dfrac{4\lambda}{d} - \dfrac{2\lambda}{d} = \dfrac{2\lambda}{d} = 6 - 3 =3cm$

Width of central maxima,$= \dfrac{2\lambda}{d} = 3\text{c}\text{m}$

44595.text: An artillery piece of mass ${M}_{1}$ fires a shell of mass ${M}_{2}$ horizontally. Instantaneously after the firing, the ratio of kinetic energy of the artillery and that of the shell is :
44595.sol:
As linear momentum will be conserved, $\left|\overset{⇀}{p}1\right| = \left|\overset{⇀}{p}2\right|$

Now, kinetic energy can be written as $KE = \dfrac{{p}^{2}}{2M}$.

Also $p$ is the same for both masses. We can write,

$KE ∝ \dfrac{1}{m}$

$⇒ \dfrac{K{E}_{1}}{K{E}_{2}} = \dfrac{\dfrac{{p}^{2}}{2{M}_{1}}}{\dfrac{{p}^{2}}{2{M}_{2}}} = \dfrac{{M}_{2}}{{M}_{1}}$

44625.subject: Physics
44625.text: A body of mass $2kg$ is initially at rest. It starts moving unidirectionally under the influence of a source of constant power $P$. Its displacement in $4s$ is $\dfrac{1}{3}{\alpha}^{2}\sqrt{P}m$. The value of $\alpha$ will be ______.
44625.sol:
Energy provided will be used to increase kinetic energy of the body. Therefore,

$\dfrac{1}{2}m{V}^{2} = Pt$

$V = \sqrt{\dfrac{2Pt}{m}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dx}{dt} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2Pt}{m}} ⇒ {∫}_{0}^{x}dx = \sqrt{\dfrac{2P}{m}}{∫}_{0}^{4}t\dfrac{1}{2}dt$

$⇒ x = \sqrt{\dfrac{2P}{m}}\dfrac{2}{3}{\left[t\dfrac{3}{2}\right]}_{0}^{4}$

$⇒ x = \dfrac{16\sqrt{P}}{3} = \dfrac{1}{3} \times 16\sqrt{P}$

Hence, required value of $\alpha = 4$.

\( $\mathrm{Q}=\mathrm{Cm} \Delta \mathrm{T}$\)

\( \Rightarrow C=$\frac{Q}{m \Delta T} \mathrm{~T}$\)
Therefore, SI unit of specific heat capacity is \( J k g^{-1} K^{-1} \)

52429.text:
Frosted glass is widely used for translucent windows. The region, where a transparent adhesive tape is stuck over the frosted glass becomes transparent. The most reasonable explanation for this is
&
options:
diffusion of adhesive glue into glass
&

chemical reaction at adhesive tape-glass interface
&

refractive index of adhesive glue is close to that of glass
&
adhesive tape is more transparent than glass
52429.sol:
Frosted glass has a rough layer which causes irregular refraction and makes glass translucent.

When a transparent tape which has refractive index close to that of glass is pasted over the rough surface of glass, the tape glue fills the roughness of glass. This makes glass surface more smooth and so refraction is more regular. This makes region of tape transparent.

55244.subject: Chemistry
55244.text:
Identify the substrate 'A' in the following reaction.
$\text{A} \xrightarrow[\large{\text{ii)}\ \Delta}]{\large{\text{i) Moist Ag}_2\text{O}}} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{N(CH}_3)_2 + \text{CH}_2 = \text{CH}_2$
55244.sol:
The given reaction is the Hofmann elimination of a quaternary ammonium salt.

Substrate A reacts with moist $\text{Ag}_2\text{O}$ to form a quaternary ammonium hydroxide, which on heating undergoes $\beta$-elimination to yield an alkene, a tertiary amine, and water.

The products obtained are $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{N(CH}_3)_2$ (N,N-dimethylethylamine) and $\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}_2$ (ethene).

The quaternary ammonium ion must contain the alkyl groups present in the tertiary amine along with the alkyl group that underwent elimination to form the alkene. Combining an ethyl group (from ethene) with N,N-dimethylethylamine gives the diethyldimethylammonium ion, $[(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2)_2\text{N}(\text{CH}_3)_2]^+$.

Since moist $\text{Ag}_2\text{O}$ is used in the first step to replace a halide ion with a hydroxide ion, substrate A must be a halide.

Therefore, substrate A is diethyldimethylammonium halide.

Answer: Diethyldimethylammonium halide

55784.subject: Chemistry
55784.text: What is the number of electrons in bonding molecular orbitals and antibonding molecular orbitals respectively in $\mathrm{F}_2$ molecule.
55784.sol:
Molecular Orbital Configuration for $\mathrm{F}_2$ The $\mathrm{F}_2$ molecule contains 18 electrons total. For diatomic molecules with more than 14 electrons, the molecular orbital filling order is: $\sigma_{1s}^2\sigma^{*}{}_{1s}^{2}\sigma_{2s}^2\sigma^{*}{}_{2s}^2\sigma_{2p_z}^2$ (\pi_{2p_x}^2 = \pi_{2p_y}^2$) (\pi^{*}{}_{2p_x}^2 = \pi^{*}{}_{2p_y}^2$) The configuration is $\sigma_{1s}^2\sigma^{*}{}_{1s}^2\sigma_{2s}^2\sigma^{*}{}_{2s}^2\sigma_{2p_z}^2\pi_{2p_x}^2\pi_{2p_y}^2\pi^{*}{}_{2p_x}^2\pi^{*}{}_{2p_y}^2$. Bonding electrons (N_b$) are in orbitals without asterisks: \sigma_{1s}^2$, $\sigma_{2s}^2$, $\sigma_{2p_z}^2$, $\pi_{2p_x}^2$, and $\pi_{2p_y}^2$ giving $2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 10$ electrons. Antibonding electrons (N_a$) are in \sigma^{*}{}_{1s}^2$, $\sigma^{*}{}_{2s}^2$, $\pi^{*}{}_{2p_x}^2$, and $\pi^{*}{}_{2p_y}^2$ giving $2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 8$ electrons.

The correct option is $\boxed{\text{B}}$.

57154.subject: Chemistry
57154.text: What type of following reactions, the oxidative rancidity is?
57154.sol:
Oxidative rancidity is the process of autoxidation of lipids (fats and oils) exposed to oxygen, resulting in unpleasant odors and flavors.

This autoxidation proceeds via a free radical chain reaction mechanism.

The mechanism involves three main steps: initiation (formation of lipid free radicals), propagation (reaction of lipid radicals with oxygen to form peroxyl radicals, which abstract hydrogen from other lipid molecules), and termination (combination of radicals to form stable, non-radical products).

Therefore, oxidative rancidity is a free radical chain reaction.

Answer: free radical chain reaction

57872.subject: Chemistry
57872.text: Identify the major product formed when 2-Methylhexan-3-ol is heated with concentrated sulphuric acid.
57872.sol:
Dehydration of 2-methylhexan-3-ol with concentrated $\mathrm{H_2 SO_4}$ proceeds via an E1 mechanism. Protonation of the hydroxyl group forms an oxonium ion, which loses water to yield a secondary carbocation at C3.

To enhance stability, a 1,2-hydride shift occurs from the adjacent carbon, converting the secondary carbocation into a tertiary carbocation at C2: $\mathrm{CH_3-C+(CH_3)-CH_2-CH_2-CH_2-CH_3}$.

Elimination follows Zaitsev's rule, favoring formation of the most substituted alkene. Deprotonation from C3 generates the trisubstituted alkene 2-methylhex-2-ene: $\mathrm{CH_3-C(CH_3)=CH-CH_2-CH_2-CH_3}$, which corresponds to option A.

The final answer is $\boxed{A}$.

58832.subject: Chemistry
58832.text: A compound forms bcc unit cell with edge length $400$ pm. Determine the molar mass of the compound if the density of compound is $3.5\ \text{g cm}^{-3}$ [N_A = 6.022 \times 10^{23}$]$
58832.sol:
The formula for the density of a unit cell is given by:

$d = \dfrac{Z \times M}{N_A \times a^3}$

For a bcc unit cell, the number of atoms per unit cell is $Z = 2$.

Given:
$d = 3.5\ \text{g cm}^{-3}$
$a = 400\ \text{pm} = 4 \times 10^{-8}\ \text{cm}$
$N_A = 6.022 \times 10^{23}\ \text{mol}^{-1}$

Rearranging the formula to solve for molar mass $M$:

$M = \dfrac{d \times N_A \times a^3}{Z}$

Substituting the given values:

$M = \dfrac{3.5 \times 6.022 \times 10^{23} \times (4 \times 10^{-8})^3}{2}$

$M = \dfrac{3.5 \times 6.022 \times 10^{23} \times 64 \times 10^{-24}}{2}$

$M = \dfrac{3.5 \times 6.022 \times 6.4}{2}$

$M = 67.4464\ \text{g mol}^{-1}$

Rounding to one decimal place, $M \approx 67.4\ \text{g mol}^{-1}$.

Answer: $67.4\ \text{g mol}^{-1}$

59101.subject: Chemistry
59101.text: Calculate the molar mass of a nonvolatile solute if 6.4 g of it dissolved in 100 g water produces a relative lowering in vapour pressure of $0 \cdot 016$ at 300 K.
59101.sol:
The relative lowering in vapour pressure is given by Raoult's law:

$\dfrac{\Delta P}{P^0} = \dfrac{n_2}{n_1 + n_2}$

For a dilute solution, $n_2 \ll n_1$, so $n_1 + n_2 \approx n_1$. The equation simplifies to:

$\dfrac{\Delta P}{P^0} \approx \dfrac{n_2}{n_1} = \dfrac{w_2 M_1}{M_2 w_1}$

Given:
Relative lowering in vapour pressure, $\dfrac{\Delta P}{P^0} = 0.016$
Mass of solute, $w_2 = 6.4 \text{ g}$
Mass of solvent (water), $w_1 = 100 \text{ g}$
Molar mass of water, $M_1 = 18 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$

Substituting the values into the formula:

$0.016 = \dfrac{6.4 \times 18}{M_2 \times 100}$

$M_2 = \dfrac{6.4 \times 18}{0.016 \times 100}$

$M_2 = \dfrac{115.2}{1.6} = 72 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$

Answer: $72 \text{ gmol}^{-1}$

59752.subject: Chemistry
59752.text: Which from following is NOT an example of oil in water emulsion?
59752.sol:
Emulsions are broadly classified into two types based on the dispersed phase and dispersion medium:

1. Oil in water (O/W) emulsion: In this type, oil acts as the dispersed phase and water acts as the dispersion medium. Examples include milk, vanishing cream, and paint.

2. Water in oil (W/O) emulsion: In this type, water acts as the dispersed phase and oil acts as the dispersion medium. Examples include butter, cold cream, and cod liver oil.

Since butter is a water in oil (W/O) emulsion, it is not an example of an oil in water emulsion.

Answer: Butter

60252.text: The rate of change of the volume of a sphere with respect to its surface area, when the radius is 5 m is
60252.sol:
Rate of Change of Volume with Respect to Surface Area

Given a sphere of radius $r$ and fixed formulas for volume $V = \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3$ and surface area $A = 4\pi r^2$, the derivative $\frac{dV}{dA}$ is determined using the chain rule as $\frac{dV}{dA} = \frac{dV/dr}{dA/dr}$.

The derivatives with respect to the radius are $\frac{dV}{dr} = 4\pi r^2$ and $\frac{dA}{dr} = 8\pi r$. Substituting into the chain rule yields $\frac{dV}{dA} = \frac{4\pi r^2}{8\pi r} = \frac{r}{2}$.

For $r = 5$ m, the result is $\frac{5}{2}$ m, which corresponds to option A.

60904.subject: Mathematics
60904.text: If the function $f(x) = \left(\dfrac{5x - 8}{8 - 3x}\right)^{\frac{3}{2x - 4}}$, for $x \neq 2$ is continuous at $x = 2$, then the value of $f(2)$ is...
60904.sol:
Since $f(x)$ is continuous at $x = 2$, $f(2) = \lim_{x \to 2} f(x)$.

$f(2) = \lim_{x \to 2} \left(\dfrac{5x - 8}{8 - 3x}\right)^{\dfrac{3}{2x - 4}}$

As $x \to 2$, the base approaches $1$ and the exponent approaches $\infty$, so this is of the form $1^{\infty}$.

Using the standard limit $\lim_{x \to a} [h(x)]^{g(x)} = e^{\lim_{x \to a} g(x)[h(x) - 1]}$ for $1^{\infty}$ form:

$f(2) = e^{\lim_{x \to 2} \dfrac{3}{2x - 4} \left(\dfrac{5x - 8}{8 - 3x} - 1\right)}$

$f(2) = e^{\lim_{x \to 2} \dfrac{3}{2(x - 2)} \left(\dfrac{5x - 8 - (8 - 3x)}{8 - 3x}\right)}$

$f(2) = e^{\lim_{x \to 2} \dfrac{3}{2(x - 2)} \left(\dfrac{8x - 16}{8 - 3x}\right)}$

$f(2) = e^{\lim_{x \to 2} \dfrac{3}{2(x - 2)} \dfrac{8(x - 2)}{8 - 3x}}$

$f(2) = e^{\lim_{x \to 2} \dfrac{12}{8 - 3x}}$

Substituting $x = 2$:

$f(2) = e^{\dfrac{12}{8 - 6}} = e^6$

Answer: $e^6$

61659.text: Let f(x) be a twice differentiable function such that $f''(x) = -f(x)$, $f'(x) = g(x)$ and $h(x) = \{f(x)\}^2 + \{g(x)\}^2$. If $h(5) = 11$, then $h(10)$ is equal to...
61659.sol:
Given $h(x) = (f(x))^2 + (g(x))^2$

Differentiating with respect to $x$:

$h'(x) = 2f(x)f'(x) + 2g(x)g'(x)$

Given $f'(x) = g(x)$, differentiating gives $f''(x) = g'(x)$.

Also given $f''(x) = -f(x)$, so $g'(x) = -f(x)$.

Substituting these into $h'(x)$:

$h'(x) = 2f(x)g(x) + 2g(x)(-f(x)) = 0$

Since $h'(x) = 0$, $h(x)$ is a constant function.

Given $h(5) = 11$, it follows that $h(10) = 11$.

Answer: $11$

62006.sol:
Let $t = \dfrac{x-1}{x+1}$

$t(x+1) = x-1$

$tx + t = x - 1$

$x(1-t) = t+1$

$x = \dfrac{t+1}{1-t}$

Substituting $x$ in the given equation:

$f(t) = \dfrac{t+1}{1-t} + 1$

$f(t) = \dfrac{t+1+1-t}{1-t} = \dfrac{2}{1-t}$

Replacing $t$ with $x$:

$f(x) = \dfrac{2}{1-x}$

Integrating with respect to $x$:

$\int f(x)\,dx = \int \dfrac{2}{1-x}\,dx$

$\int f(x)\,dx = -2\log|1-x| + c$

Answer: $-2\log|1 - x| + c$

63594.subject: Mathematics
63594.text: The odds in favour of A winning a game of table tennis against B are 1:2. If 3 games are to be played, then the probability of A winning at least two games out of the three is.....
63594.sol:
Given odds in favour of A winning are $1:2$.

Probability of A winning a game is $p = \dfrac{1}{1+2} = \dfrac{1}{3}$.

Probability of A losing a game is $q = 1 - p = \dfrac{2}{3}$.

Total number of games played is $n = 3$.

Probability of A winning at least two games is $P(X \ge 2) = P(X = 2) + P(X = 3)$.

Using binomial distribution, $P(X = r) = ^{n}C_{r} p^{r} q^{n-r}$.

$P(X \ge 2) = ^{3}C_{2} \left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)^{2} \left(\dfrac{2}{3}\right)^{1} + ^{3}C_{3} \left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)^{3} \left(\dfrac{2}{3}\right)^{0}$

$P(X \ge 2) = 3 \times \dfrac{1}{9} \times \dfrac{2}{3} + 1 \times \dfrac{1}{27} \times 1$

$P(X \ge 2) = \dfrac{6}{27} + \dfrac{1}{27} = \dfrac{7}{27}$

Answer: $\dfrac{7}{27}$

63959.subject: Mathematics
63959.text: In $\triangle ABC$ with usual notations, if $1 + \tan\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right)\tan\left(\dfrac{B}{2}\right) = \dfrac{k}{s}$ (where $s$ is the semi-perimeter), then the value of $k$ is...
63959.sol:
Using the half-angle formulas for a triangle:

$\tan\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right) = \sqrt{\dfrac{(s-b)(s-c)}{s(s-a)}}$

$\tan\left(\dfrac{B}{2}\right) = \sqrt{\dfrac{(s-a)(s-c)}{s(s-b)}}$

Multiplying these two expressions:

$\tan\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right)\tan\left(\dfrac{B}{2}\right) = \sqrt{\dfrac{(s-b)(s-c)}{s(s-a)} \dfrac{(s-a)(s-c)}{s(s-b)}} = \dfrac{s-c}{s}$

Substituting this into the given equation:

$1 + \tan\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right)\tan\left(\dfrac{B}{2}\right) = 1 + \dfrac{s-c}{s} = \dfrac{2s - c}{s}$

Since $2s = a + b + c$, we have $2s - c = a + b$.

Therefore, $1 + \tan\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right)\tan\left(\dfrac{B}{2}\right) = \dfrac{a + b}{s}$

Comparing this with $\dfrac{k}{s}$, we get $k = a + b$.

Answer: $a + b$

65533.subject: Physics
65533.text: Given below are the two circuits, choose the correct option.
options: At resonance, current in (B) is less than that in (A)
The r.m.s. current in (B) can be larger than that in (A)
The r.m.s. current in (A) is always equal to that in (B)
The r.m.s. current in (B) can never be larger than that in (A)
65533.sol:
For circuit (A), the impedance is purely resistive:

$Z_A = R = 30\ \Omega$

The r.m.s. current in circuit (A) is:

$I_A = \dfrac{V_{rms}}{Z_A} = \dfrac{V_{rms}}{R}$

For circuit (B), which is a series LCR circuit, the impedance is given by:

$Z_B = \sqrt{R^2 + (X_L - X_C)^2}$

Since the square of any real number is non-negative, $(X_L - X_C)^2 \ge 0$. Therefore, the impedance of circuit (B) will always be greater than or equal to the resistance $R$:

$Z_B \ge R$

$Z_B \ge Z_A$

The r.m.s. current in circuit (B) is:

$I_B = \dfrac{V_{rms}}{Z_B}$

Since $V_{rms}$ is the same for both circuits ($210\text{ V}$) and $Z_B \ge Z_A$, it follows that:

$I_B \le I_A$

At resonance, $X_L = X_C$, which gives $Z_B = R$ and $I_B = I_A$. For all other conditions, $Z_B > R$ and $I_B < I_A$.

Thus, the r.m.s. current in (B) can never be larger than that in (A).

Answer: The r.m.s. current in (B) can never be larger than that in (A)

66326.text: In metre-bridge experiment the balance point is obtained if the gaps are closed by $2 \Omega$ and $3 \Omega$. A shunt of $x \Omega$ is added to $3 \Omega$ resistor to shift the balance point by 22.5 cm. The value of x is
66326.sol:
The metre bridge operates on the Wheatstone bridge principle, with the balance condition $\frac{R_1}{R_2} = \frac{l}{100 - l}$ where $l$ is the length from the $R_1$ side.

With $R_1 = 2\ \Omega$ and $R_2 = 3\ \Omega$, the initial balance point satisfies $\frac{2}{3} = \frac{l}{100 - l}$, yielding $l = 40$ cm.

When a shunt resistance $x$ is added in parallel to $3\ \Omega$, the equivalent resistance becomes $R_2' = \frac{3x}{x + 3}$.

The balance point shifts by 22.5 cm to $l' = 62.5$ cm. The new balance condition gives $\frac{2}{\frac{3x}{x + 3}} = \frac{62.5}{37.5}$, which simplifies to $\frac{2(x + 3)}{3x} = \frac{5}{3}$.

Solving $2(x + 3) = 5x$ yields $x = 2\ \Omega$.

Final answer: $\boxed{B}$

67659.subject: Physics
67659.text: Lorentz magnetic force is acting on a particle of charge $q$ moving with velocity $\vec{V}$ in magnetic field $\vec{B}$. The work done by this force on the charged particle is
67659.sol:
The Lorentz magnetic force on a charged particle is given by $\vec{F} = q(\vec{V} \times \vec{B})$.

The power delivered by this force is $P = \vec{F} \cdot \vec{V} = q(\vec{V} \times \vec{B}) \cdot \vec{V}$.

Since the cross product $\vec{V} \times \vec{B}$ is always perpendicular to the velocity vector $\vec{V}$, their dot product is zero.

Thus, $P = 0$.

The work done by the magnetic force is $W = \int P dt = 0$.

Therefore, the work done by the Lorentz magnetic force on the charged particle is zero.

Answer: zero

67802.subject: Physics
67802.text: A wire of length $L$ carries a current $i$. If the wire is turned into a circular coil and kept in a uniform magnetic field $B$, the maximum magnitude of torque in the given magnetic field will be
67802.sol:
The torque on the current loop is $\tau=N I A B \sin \alpha---(1)$ If there are $N$ turns of the circular coil, each of radius $r$, then $L=2 \pi r N\Rightarrow r=\frac{L}{2 \pi N}$
Area of the coil, $A=\pi r^2=\pi\left(\frac{L}{2 \pi N}\right)^2=\frac{L^2}{4 \pi N^2}$ Putting this value in (1), we get,
$\tau=N I\left(\frac{L^2}{4 \pi N^2}\right) B \sin \alpha=\frac{L^2 I B \sin \alpha}{4 \pi N}--(2)$
From (2), it is clear that $\tau$ is maximum if $N$ is minimum. Torque is maximum if $\sin \alpha=1$ and $N=1\therefore \tau_{\max }=L^2 I B / 4 \pi$

68136.text: The liquid (mercury) meniscus in capillary tube will be convex if the angle of contact is
68136.sol:
The shape of a liquid meniscus in a capillary tube is governed by the angle of contact $\theta$, defined as the angle between the tangent to the liquid surface at the point of contact and the solid surface, measured within the liquid.

For mercury in glass, the meniscus appears convex, indicating that cohesive forces within the liquid exceed adhesive forces between the liquid and solid. This corresponds to an obtuse angle of contact: $\theta > 90^{{}^{\circ}}$.

$\therefore$ The correct option is A.

69739.subject: Physics
69739.text: A liquid having coefficient of cubical expansion ' $\gamma$ ' is kept in a copper vessel having coefficient of linear expansion $\frac{\gamma}{3}$. If heat is supplied to the vessel, the original level of the liquid in the vessel will
69739.sol:
The coefficient of cubical expansion of the liquid is $\gamma_L = \gamma$, while the vessel's coefficient of linear expansion is $\alpha_V = \frac{\gamma}{3}$.
The cubical expansion coefficient for the vessel becomes $\gamma_V = 3\alpha_V = 3\left(\frac{\gamma}{3}\right) = \gamma$.

Given equal initial volumes $V_0$ and temperature change $\Delta T$,
the liquid expands by $\Delta V_L = V_0 \gamma \Delta T$ and the vessel's internal volume by $\Delta V_V = V_0 \gamma \Delta T$,
resulting in zero apparent volume change: $\Delta V_\text{app} = V_0(\gamma - \gamma)\Delta T = 0$.

The liquid level remains constant: $\boxed{C}$.

69973.subject: Physics
69973.text: Three samples $\mathrm{X}, \mathrm{Y}$, and Z of same gas have equal volumes and temperatures. The volume of each sample is doubled, the process being isothermal for X, adiabatic for Y and isobaric for Z. If the final pressures are equal for the three samples, the ratio of the initial pressures is $(r=3 / 2)$
69973.sol:
Initial Pressures for Volume Expansion Processes

Let $V_0$ be the initial volume and $V_f = 2V_0$ the final volume for all samples. Final pressure is $P_f$ for each. Given $\gamma = 3/2$.

For the isothermal process (Sample X), since $PV$ is constant:

$P_X V_0 = P_f (2V_0)$

$P_X = 2P_f$

For the adiabatic process (Sample Y), as $PV^\gamma$ is constant:

$P_Y V_0^{3/2} = P_f (2V_0)^{3/2}$

$P_Y = P_f \cdot 2^{3/2} = 2\sqrt{2} P_f$

In the isobaric process (Sample Z), pressure remains constant:

$P_Z = P_f$

The ratio of initial pressures is:

$P_X : P_Y : P_Z = 2P_f : 2\sqrt{2}P_f : P_f = 2 : 2\sqrt{2} : 1$

This corresponds to option B.

71398.subject: Biology
71398.text: The daughter of a colour- blind father and a normal mother marries a normal male. What percentage of male children of this couple will be colour -blind ?
71398.sol:
Colour blindness is an X-linked recessive disorder.

Genotype of the colour-blind father: $X^c Y$

Genotype of the normal mother: $X^C X^C$

The daughter receives the $X^c$ chromosome from her father and the $X^C$ chromosome from her mother. Thus, her genotype is $X^C X^c$ (carrier).

She marries a normal male, whose genotype is $X^C Y$.

The cross between the carrier female (X^C X^c$) and the normal male (X^C Y$) produces the following offspring:

Male children receive their X chromosome from the mother and Y chromosome from the father.

The mother produces two types of eggs: $X^C$ and $X^c$ in equal proportions.

Therefore, the male children will be $X^C Y$ (normal) and $X^c Y$ (colour-blind) in a $1:1$ ratio.

Hence, $50\%$ of the male children will be colour-blind.

Answer: 50 %

71970.subject: Chemistry
71970.text: Which of the following aqueous solutions exhibits maximum freezing point depression assuming complete dissociation?
71970.sol:
The depression in freezing point is given by $\Delta T_f = i \times K_f \times m$.

Since $K_f$ is constant for aqueous solutions, $\Delta T_f \propto i \times m$.

For $0.1$ m $\text{Li}_2\text{SO}_4$, $i = 3$, $i \times m = 3 \times 0.1 = 0.3$

For $0.5$ m KCl, $i = 2$, $i \times m = 2 \times 0.5 = 1.0$

For $0.05$ m $\text{Al}_2(\text{SO}_4)_3$, $i = 5$, $i \times m = 5 \times 0.05 = 0.25$

For $0.2$ m $\text{BaCl}_2$, $i = 3$, $i \times m = 3 \times 0.2 = 0.6$

The maximum value of $i \times m$ is $1.0$ for $0.5$ m KCl, which will exhibit the maximum freezing point depression.

Answer: $0.5$ m KCl.

71976.subject: Chemistry
71976.text: 200 mL of an aqueous solution of a protein contain $1.26$ g of protein, the osmotic pressure of this solution at 300 K is found to be $2.57 \times 10^{-3}$ bar, Calculate the molar mass of protein. ( R = 0.083 bar mol^{-1}$ K^{-1}$)
71976.sol:
Given:
Volume of solution, $V = 200$ mL $= 0.200$ L
Mass of protein, $W = 1.26$ g
Osmotic pressure, $\pi = 2.57 \times 10^{-3}$ bar
Temperature, $T = 300$ K
Gas constant, $R = 0.083$ L bar K^{-1}$ mol^{-1}$

Using the formula for osmotic pressure:
$\pi = \dfrac{W}{M V} R T$

Rearranging for molar mass $M$:
$M = \dfrac{W R T}{\pi V}$

Substituting the values:
$M = \dfrac{1.26 \times 0.083 \times 300}{2.57 \times 10^{-3} \times 0.200}$

$M = \dfrac{31.374}{5.14 \times 10^{-4}}$

$M = 61038.9$ g mol^{-1} \approx 61039$ g mol^{-1}$

Answer: $61039$ g mol^{-1}

72408.subject: Physics
72408.text: A clock with an iron pendulum keeps the correct time at $14^{}^{\circ}\text{C}$. If the room temperature is $20^{}^{\circ}\text{C}$, the error in a second per day will be nearly (coefficient of linear expansion of iron is $1.2 \times 10^{-5} / {}^{}^{\circ}\text{C}$ )
72408.sol:
The time period of a simple pendulum is given by $T = 2\pi \sqrt{\dfrac{L}{g}}$

Fractional change in time period due to temperature change is $\dfrac{\Delta T}{T} = \dfrac{1}{2} \alpha \Delta \theta$

Error in time per day is $\Delta t = \dfrac{1}{2} \alpha \Delta \theta \times t$

where $t = 24 \times 60 \times 60 = 86400 \text{ s}$

Given $\alpha = 1.2 \times 10^{-5} / ^{}^{\circ}\text{C}$ and $\Delta \theta = 20^{}^{\circ}\text{C} - 14^{}^{\circ}\text{C} = 6^{}^{\circ}\text{C}$

Substituting the values:

$\Delta t = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 1.2 \times 10^{-5} \times 6 \times 86400$

$\Delta t = 3.6 \times 10^{-5} \times 86400 = 3.1104 \text{ s}$

The error per day is approximately $3.11 \text{ s}$.

Answer: $3.11 \text{ s}$

Paragraph: There was a farewell ceremony on her day at school, to which my parents and I were invited. It was a touching ceremony in a solemn kind of way. The City Corporation sent a representative and so did the two main political parties. There were many speeches and my grandmother was garlanded by a girl from every class. Then the head-girl, a particular favourite of hers, unveiled the farewell present the girls had bought for her by subscription. It was a large marble model of the Taj Mahal; it had a bulb inside and could be lit up like a table lamp. My grandmother made a speech too, but she couldn't finish it properly, for she began to cry before she got to the end of it and to stop to wipe away her tears. I turned away when she began dabbing at her eyes with a huge green handkerchief, and discovered, to my surprise, that many of the girls sitting around me were wiping their eyes too. I was very jealous, I remember. I had always taken it for granted that it was my own special right to love her; I did not know how to cope with the discovery that my right had been infringed by a whole school.

By lens formula

$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \frac{1}{\mathrm{u}}-\frac{1}{10}=\frac{1}{5} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{1}{\mathrm{u}}=\frac{1-2}{10} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{1}{\mathrm{u}}=\frac{1}{10} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{u}=-10\end{aligned}$
So, $m=\frac{v}{u}=\frac{-5}{-10}=\frac{1}{2}=0.5$

77279.sol:
Let ellipse be $\frac{x^2}{a^2}+\frac{y^2}{b^2}=1$
It's foci are $\mathrm{S}_1(a e, o)$ and $\mathrm{S}_2(-a e, o)$ and the extremity of the minor axis is $\mathrm{B}(o, b)$ Then, slope of $\mathrm{BS}_2=\frac{b-o}{o-(-a e)}=\frac{b}{a e}$ and $\quad$ slope of $\mathrm{BS}_1=\frac{b-o}{o-a e}=-\frac{b}{a e}$ The product of slopes $=\frac{b}{a e} \times-\frac{b}{a e}=-1\Rightarrow \quad b^2=a^2 e^2\Rightarrow \quad e^2=\frac{b^2}{a^2} \qquad$ ....(i) We have,$e=\frac{c}{a}\Rightarrow \quad c=\sqrt{a^2-b^2}\Rightarrow \quad e^2=1-\frac{b^2}{a^2}=1-e^2 \quad[$ from $(i)]\begin{aligned} \Rightarrow & & 2 e^2 & =1 \\ \Rightarrow & & e^2 & =\frac{1}{2} \Rightarrow e=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}$

Let first term of G.P. is $a$ and common ratio $=r\because 10^{\text{th }}$ term of G.P. is 9
$\Rightarrow \quad a r^9=9$ ...(i)
and
$a r^3=4$ (ii)
Divide (i) by (ii)
$\frac{a r^9}{a r^3}=\frac{9}{4} \Rightarrow r^6=\frac{9}{4}\Rightarrow \quad\left(r^3\right)^2=\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^2r^3=\frac{3}{2}$
Putting the value of $r^3$ in (i)

80143.subject: Botany
80143.text: How many turns of Calvin cycle are required for the formation of three molecules of glucose ?
80143.sol:
One turn of the Calvin cycle fixes one molecule of $CO_2$.

To synthesize one molecule of glucose ($C_6H_{12}O_6$), six molecules of $CO_2$ are required.

Thus, six turns of the Calvin cycle are required to produce one molecule of glucose.

For the formation of three molecules of glucose, the number of turns required is $3 \times 6 = 18$.

Answer: $18$

E.M.F. diagram for some ions is given as
$Fe{O}_{4}^{2 -}\overset{E^{o} = + 2.20V}{→}Fe^{3 +}\overset{E^{o} = + 0.77V}{→}Fe^{2 +}\overset{E^{o} = - 0.445V}{→}Fe^{o}$

88133.sol:
$Fe^{6 +} + 3e \to Fe^{3 +};- \Delta{G}_{1}^{o} = 3 \times 2.20 \times F$ …(i)
$Fe^{3 +} + e \to Fe^{2 +};- \Delta{G}_{2}^{o} = 1 \times 0.77 \times F$ …(ii)
$Fe^{2 +} + 2e \to Fe^{o};- \Delta{G}_{3}^{o} = 2 \times ( - 0.445 ) \times F$ …(iii)
By equation (i) and (ii)
$Fe^{6 +} + 4e \to Fe^{2 +};- \Delta{G}_{4}^{o} = - \Delta{G}_{1}^{o} - \Delta{G}_{2}^{o}$
Hence $4 \times {E}_{4}^{o} \times F = 3 \times 2.20 \times F + \left(1 \times0.77 \timesF\right)$
So ${E}_{4}^{o} = 1.84V$
or $Fe^{6 +} + 4e \to Fe^{2 +};E^{o} = 1.84V
$

90628.text: The differential equation of the family of curves whose tangent at any point makes an angle of $\dfrac{\pi}{4}$ with the ellipse $\dfrac{x^{2}}{4} + y^{2} = 1$ is
90628.sol:
Given, $\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{4} + {y}^{2} = 1$

On differentiating w.r.t. $x$,

$\dfrac{x}{2} + 2y\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{- x}{4y} = {m}_{1}\left(let\right)$

Let, the slope of the tangent at a point on ellipse where the tangents meet is ${m}_{2}$

Given, $tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = \left|\dfrac{{m}_{1} - {m}_{2}}{1 + {m}_{1}{m}_{2}}\right|$

$1 = \left|\dfrac{- \dfrac{x}{4y} - {m}_{2}}{1 + \dfrac{x}{4y}{m}_{2}}\right| ⇒ \left|4y - x{m}_{2}\right| = \left|x + 4y{m}_{2}\right|$

$4y - x{m}_{2} = x + 4y{m}_{2}$ or $4y - x{m}_{2} = - x - 4y{m}_{2}$

${m}_{2} = \dfrac{4y - x}{x + 4y}$ or ${m}_{2} = \dfrac{4y + x}{x - 4y}$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{4y - x}{x + 4y}$ or $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{4y + x}{x - 4y}$

The total cases$= {5}^{3}$

The possible cases are $\left(2, 1,1\right), \left(3, 1, 2\right), \left(3, 2, 1\right)$, $\left(4,1, 3\right) \left(4,3, 1\right), \left(4,2, 2\right)$, $\left(5,3, 2\right)\left(5,2, 3\right)$, $\left(5,4, 1\right)\left(5,1, 4\right)$

91688.text: Suppose that the side lengths of a triangle are three consecutive integers and one of the angles is twice another. The number of such triangles is/are
91688.sol:
Let $\text{B} = 2\text{A}$ and $\text{B}\text{D}$ be the bisector of angle $\text{B}$, then

$\text{CD} = \dfrac{\text{ab}}{\text{a} + \text{c}} \text{$ and $} \text{AD} = \dfrac{\text{bc}}{\text{a} + \text{c}}$

Now,  $\Delta \text{ABC}$ and \Delta $\text{BDC}$ are similar, so

$\dfrac{\text{BC}}{\text{AC}} = \dfrac{\text{CD}}{\text{BC}} ⇒ {\text{a}}^{2} = \dfrac{\text{ab}}{\text{a} + \text{c}} \text{b} ⇒ {\text{b}}^{2} = \text{a} \left(\text{a}$ + $\text{c}\right)     ......(i)

Since, \text{b} > \text{a} ⇒$ Either $\text{b} = \text{a} +1$ or $\text{b} = \text{a} +2,$ if $\text{b} = \text{a} +$1,$ then [From Eq.(i)]

${$\left(\text{a} +1\right)$}^{2} = $\left(\text{a} + \text{c}\right) \text{a} ⇒ \text{c} =2 + \dfrac{1}{\text{a}}$

 
$\text{c} i$s integer $⇒ \text{a} =1, \text{b} =2, \text{c} =3$ but then, no triangle will form.
If $\text{b} = \text{a} +$2,$ then obviously \text{c} = \text{a} +1,$ and then, [from Eq. (i)]

${\left(\text{a}$ +2\right)$}^{2} = $$\text{a}$\left(2 $\text{a}$ +1\right)

$⇒ {$$\text{a}$$}^{2} - 3a - 4 = 0 $$\text{or}$$\text{a}$=$4$

$∴ $$\text{a}$$ =4, $$\text{b}$$ =6, $$\text{c}$$ =5$ is the only possible solution.

92055.text: A variable line through the point $\left(\dfrac{6}{5}, \dfrac{6}{5}\right)$ cuts the coordinate axes at the points $A and B$ respectively. If the point $P$ divides $AB$ internally in the ratio $2: 1,$ then the equation of the locus of $P$ is

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{a} + \dfrac{1}{b} = \dfrac{5}{6}$
Let, $P = \left(h, k\right)$, then

$h = \dfrac{2\left(0\right) + 1\left(a\right)}{3} = \dfrac{a}{3}$ & $k = \dfrac{2\left(b\right) + 1\left(0\right)}{3} = \dfrac{2b}{3}$
$⇒ a = 3h$ & $b = 3\dfrac{k}{2}$
$⇒ \dfrac{1}{3h} + \dfrac{2}{3k} = \dfrac{5}{6}$
$⇒$ locus of $P$ is $2\left(y + 2x\right) = 5xy$

92202.text: A plane $P = 0$ passes through the line of intersection of the planes~$x + y + z + 3 = 0 and x - y + z - 2 = 0$. If the plane $P$ divides the line joining $\left(3, 0, 2\right) and \left(0, 3, - 1\right) in the ratio $2: 1$ internally and the~ equation of the plane is $ax - 2y + bz = c$ where $a, b, c \in N$, then the value of~$3a + 4b - 5c$ is equal to$
92202.sol:
The equation of the plane is $\left(x + y + z + 3\right) + \lambda\left(x - y + z - 2\right) = 0$
$⇒ x\left(1 + \lambda\right) + y\left(1 - \lambda\right) + z\left(1 + \lambda\right) + 3 - 2\lambda = 0$
A point which divides $\left(3, 0, 2\right)$ and $\left(0, 3, - 1\right)$ in $2: 1$ internally is

$\left(\dfrac{2 \times 0 + 1 \times 3}{3}, \dfrac{2 \times 3 + 0 \times 1}{3}, \dfrac{2 \times \left(- 1\right) + 1 \times 2}{3}\right)$
$≡ \left(1, 2, 0\right)$
This point must satisfy the equation of the plane

$⇒ 1 + \lambda + 2 - 2\lambda + 0 + 3 - 2\lambda = 0$
$⇒ 6 - 3\lambda = 0 ⇒ \lambda = 2$
Equation of the required plane is $3x - y + 3z - 1 = 0$
$⇒ 6x - 2y + 6z = 2$
$⇒ a = 6, b = 6, c = 2$
Hence, $3a + 4b - 5c = 18 + 24 - 10 = 32$

92465.text: An $AC$ circuit drawing power from a source of angular frequency $50rads^{- 1}$ has a power factor of $\text{0.6}$. In this condition, a resistance of $100Ω$& is present and the current is lagging behind the voltage. If a capacitor is connected in series, then the required capacitance that will result in a power factor of unity is
92465.sol:
As the current lags the voltage, the circuit must contain a combination of resistance and inductance.

Power factor $cos ⁡ ϕ = 0.6$

$⇒ \dfrac{R}{R^{2} + {X}_L^{2}} = \text{0.6}$

$⇒ R^{2} + {X}_L^{2} = \left(\dfrac{R}{0.6}\right)^{2}$

$⇒ {X}_L^{2} = \dfrac{R2}{\left(\text{0.6}\right)^{2}} - R^{2}$

$⇒ {X}_L^{2} = \dfrac{R^{2} \times \text{0.64}}{0.36}$

$∴ {X}_{L} = \dfrac{0.8 R}{0.6} = \dfrac{4R}{3}$

Now we want the power factor $cos ⁡ ϕ = 1$

This is the condition of resonance in which

${X}_{L} = {X}_{C}$

$∴ {X}_{C} = \dfrac{4R}{3}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{ωC} = \dfrac{4R}{3}$

$⇒ C = \dfrac{3}{4 \times 50 \times 100} = 150\mu F$

$∴ eV = \dfrac{h^{2}}{2m. {\lambda}^{2}} ⇒ \lambda = \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2meV}}$....... (iii)

When proton of mas $M$ is accelerated through a potential difference of $9V$, then the de - Broglie wavelength obtained is

${λ}^{′} = \dfrac{h}{2Me\left(9V\right)} = \dfrac{h}{3 \times \sqrt{2MeV}} \times \dfrac{m}{m}$

$∴ {\lambda}^{′} = \dfrac{\lambda}{3}. \sqrt{\dfrac{m}{M}}$

95267.subject: Botany
95267.text: Cells of ________ tissue are living, show angular wall thickenings and provide mechanical support.
95267.sol:
Collenchyma, part of the ground tissue, is a simple living tissue found in plants. Collenchyma layer is generally found below epidermis of the plant. They are either found in a patch manner or even distributed throughout. The cell wall of collenchyma tissue cells is thickened at corner due to higher deposition of cellulose, pectin and hemicellulose. The cells are generally spherical or polygonal in shape. This tissue provides mechanical support to the young stem and leaf.

Parenchyma is a type of simple permanent tissues forming a major component of the tissues of plant. These cells are in various shapes like oval, round, polygonal etc. with a thin cell wall made of cellulose. These cells perform functions like storage, photosynthesis, secretion.

The simple permanent tissue consisting of dead cells without protoplast is called sclerenchyma. These cells are long and narrow with lignified cell wall. The thick-walled, elongated pointed cells form the sclerenchyma fibres and the spherical, oval shaped cell with highly thickened cell wall and narrow cavity form the sclerenchyma sclereids.

96746.subject: Botany
96746.text:
Which of the following statements about the nitrogen cycle are false?

$1.$ Rhizobium and Frankia cause nitrogen fixation in their independent free-living stage.
$2.$ Azotobacter and Anabaena are anaerobic, symbiotic, free-living, nitrogen fixers.
$3.$ Rhodospirillum is an aerobic, nitrogen-fixing microbe found in the root nodules of legumes.
$4.$ Nitrobacter oxidizes nitrites to nitrates.
96746.sol: Free living nitrogen fixing aerobic microbes are Azobacter and Beijerinckia while Rhodospirillum is anaerobic and free living. Cyanobacteria such as Nostoc are also free living nitrogen fixers. Rhizobium has a symbiotic relationship with roots of legumes like, pea, lentils, alfalfa etc. They produce nodules on the roots. Similar to this is Frankia which also produces nitrogen fixing nodules on the roots of non-leguminous plant Alnus. Ammonia is first oxidised to nitrite by the bacteria Nitrosomonas and/or Nitrococcus. The nitrite is further oxidised to nitrate with the help of the bacterium Nitrobacter. These steps are called nitrification.

97316.subject: Botany
97316.sol: Gibberellic acid (GA_{3}) was one of the first gibberellins to be discovered and remains the most intensively studied form. All GAs are acidic. They produce a wide range of physiological responses in the plants. Their ability to cause an increase in length of axis is used to increase the length of grapes stalks. Gibberellins, cause fruits like apple to elongate and improve its shape. They also delay senescence. Thus, the fruits can be left on the tree longer so as to extend the market period. GA_{3} is used to speed up the malting process in brewing industry. Sugarcane stores carbohydrate as sugar in their stems. Spraying sugarcane crop with gibberellins increases the length of the stem, thus increasing the yield by as much as 20 tonnes per acre. Spraying juvenile conifers with GAs hastens the maturity period, thus leading to early seed production. Gibberellins also promotes bolting (internode elongation just prior to flowering) in beet, cabbages and many plants with rosette habit.

101873.subject: Physics
101873.text: A lake is freezing in a region where the steady outside air temperature is $-\theta^{\circ}\text{C}$. The density of ice is $\rho$ and its specific latent heat of fusion is $L$. A graph is plotted showing the square of the ice thickness ($x^2$) on the y-axis against time ($t$) on the x-axis. If the graph is a straight line passing through the origin with a slope $m$, the thermal conductivity of the ice is given by:
101873.sol:
The rate of heat conduction through the ice layer is equal to the rate of heat released during freezing.

$\dfrac{KA\theta}{x} = \dfrac{dm}{dt} L$

Since $dm = \rho A dx$, we have:

$\dfrac{KA\theta}{x} = \rho A L \dfrac{dx}{dt}$

$\Rightarrow \dfrac{dx}{dt} = \dfrac{K\theta}{\rho L x}$

Integrating both sides with respect to time:

$\int x \, dx = \int \dfrac{K\theta}{\rho L} \, dt$

$\dfrac{x^2}{2} = \dfrac{K\theta}{\rho L} t$

$\Rightarrow x^2 = \left(\dfrac{2K\theta}{\rho L}\right) t$

Comparing this with the equation of a straight line passing through the origin, $y = mt$, the slope $m$ of the $x^2$ versus $t$ graph is:

$m = \dfrac{2K\theta}{\rho L}$

Rearranging for the thermal conductivity $K$, we get:

$K = \dfrac{m\rho L}{2\theta}$

Answer: $\dfrac{m\rho L}{2\theta}$

102238.subject: Physics
102238.text:
Match the types of gases in List-I with their corresponding theoretical values of the ratio of specific heats $\gamma = \dfrac{C_p}{C_v}$ in List-II.

List-IList-II
(A) Monoatomic gas(I) $\dfrac{5}{3}$
(B) Diatomic gas (rigid rotor)(II) $\dfrac{7}{5}$
(C) Diatomic gas (with 1 active vibrational mode)(III) $\dfrac{9}{7}$
(D) Non-linear polyatomic gas (rigid, no vibrational mode)(IV) $\dfrac{4}{3}$


Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
102238.sol:
The ratio of specific heats is given by $\gamma = \dfrac{C_p}{C_v} = 1 + \dfrac{R}{C_v}$.

(A) Monoatomic gas: Has 3 translational degrees of freedom. $C_v = \dfrac{3}{2}R$.
$\gamma = 1 + \dfrac{2}{3} = \dfrac{5}{3}$.

(B) Diatomic gas (rigid rotor): Has 3 translational and 2 rotational degrees of freedom. $C_v = \dfrac{5}{2}R$.
$\gamma = 1 + \dfrac{2}{5} = \dfrac{7}{5}$.

(C) Diatomic gas (with 1 active vibrational mode): Has 3 translational, 2 rotational, and 1 vibrational mode. The vibrational mode contributes $R$ to $C_v$.
$C_v = \dfrac{5}{2}R + R = \dfrac{7}{2}R$.
$\gamma = 1 + \dfrac{2}{7} = \dfrac{9}{7}$.

(D) Non-linear polyatomic gas (rigid): Has 3 translational and 3 rotational degrees of freedom. $C_v = \dfrac{6}{2}R = 3R$.
$\gamma = 1 + \dfrac{1}{3} = \dfrac{4}{3}$.

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(I), (B)-(II), (C)-(III), (D)-(IV).

Answer: (A)-(I), (B)-(II), (C)-(III), (D)-(IV)

104457.subject: Physics
104457.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In an astronomical telescope, the length of the telescope tube is maximum when the final image is formed at the least distance of distinct vision.
Reason (R): For the final image to form at the least distance of distinct vision, the intermediate image formed by the objective must lie between the eyepiece and its principal focus.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
104457.sol:
The length of an astronomical telescope tube is given by $L = f_o + u_e$, where $u_e$ is the distance of the intermediate image from the eyepiece.

In normal adjustment (final image at infinity), the intermediate image is formed at the principal focus of the eyepiece, so $u_e = f_e$.

When the final image is formed at the least distance of distinct vision ($D$), the eyepiece acts as a simple magnifier forming a virtual, erect (with respect to the intermediate image) and magnified image. For a convex lens to form a virtual image, the object must lie between the optical centre and the principal focus. Thus, $u_e < f_e$. This makes Reason (R) true.

Since $u_e$ is smaller than $f_e$ in this adjustment, the tube length $L = f_o + u_e$ is minimum at the near point adjustment, whereas it is maximum in normal adjustment. Therefore, Assertion (A) is false.

Answer: (A) is false but (R) is true.

108624.subject: Chemistry
108624.text:
In which of the following processes does the entropy of the system decrease?
I. Freezing of water to ice at $0^{\circ}\text{C}$
II. $\text{N}_2(\text{g}) + 3\text{H}_2(\text{g}) \rightarrow 2\text{NH}_3(\text{g})$
III. Dissolution of solid $\text{NaCl}$ in water
IV. Heating an ideal gas from $300\text{ K}$ to $500\text{ K}$ at constant volume

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
108624.sol:
Evaluate the entropy change ($\Delta S$) for each process:

I. Freezing of water to ice involves a phase change from liquid to solid. The molecules become more ordered, so entropy decreases ($\Delta S < 0$).

II. In the reaction $\text{N}_2(\text{g}) + 3\text{H}_2(\text{g}) \rightarrow 2\text{NH}_3(\text{g})$, the number of gaseous moles decreases from 4 to 2. This leads to a decrease in randomness, so entropy decreases ($\Delta S < 0$).

III. Dissolution of solid $\text{NaCl}$ in water breaks the crystalline lattice into free-moving aqueous ions, increasing randomness. Thus, entropy increases ($\Delta S > 0$).

IV. Heating an ideal gas increases the kinetic energy and thermal randomness of the molecules, leading to an increase in entropy ($\Delta S > 0$).

Therefore, entropy decreases in processes I and II only.

Answer: I and II only

Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): $\mathrm{Ce}^{4+}$ is widely used as a good analytical reagent in aqueous medium.
Reason (R): The oxidation of water by $\mathrm{Ce}^{4+}$ is kinetically very slow.

options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
117099.sol:

Reason (R) is true and explains Assertion (A): The standard electrode potential for the $\mathrm{Ce}^{4+}/\mathrm{Ce}^{3+}$ couple is $+1.74\text{ V}$, which indicates that thermodynamically it can oxidise water. However, the reaction rate is kinetically very slow. Because this oxidation of water is so slow, aqueous solutions of $\mathrm{Ce}^{4+}$ are sufficiently stable to be used as analytical reagents.

Thus, both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

119869.subject: Chemistry
119869.text: When N-ethylethanamine is treated with benzenesulphonyl chloride and the resulting mixture is shaken with aqueous NaOH, what is the expected observation?
options: A solid is formed which dissolves in aqueous NaOH.
No reaction occurs with benzenesulphonyl chloride.
A solid is formed which remains insoluble in aqueous NaOH.
A clear solution is formed immediately upon adding benzenesulphonyl chloride.
119869.sol:
N-ethylethanamine ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{NHCH}_2\text{CH}_3$) is a secondary ($2^{\circ}$) amine.

Secondary amines react with Hinsberg's reagent (benzenesulphonyl chloride) to form N,N-dialkylbenzenesulphonamides.

Since N,N-diethylbenzenesulphonamide does not contain any hydrogen atom attached to the nitrogen atom, it is not acidic and therefore remains insoluble in aqueous alkali (NaOH).

Primary amines form a solid soluble in alkali, while tertiary amines do not react with Hinsberg's reagent to form stable sulphonamides.

Answer: A solid is formed which remains insoluble in aqueous NaOH.

119880.subject: Chemistry
119880.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Reduction of methyl isocyanide with $\text{LiAlH}_4$ yields a secondary amine, whereas reduction of ethanenitrile yields a primary amine.

Reason (R): In methyl isocyanide, the carbon atom of the isocyano group is directly attached to the methyl group.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
119880.sol:
Assertion (A) is true: Reduction of methyl isocyanide ($\text{CH}_3\text{NC}$) with $\text{LiAlH}_4$ yields N-methylmethanamine ($\text{CH}_3\text{NHCH}_3$), which is a secondary amine. Reduction of ethanenitrile ($\text{CH}_3\text{CN}$) yields ethanamine ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$), which is a primary amine.

Reason (R) is false: In isocyanides ($\text{R-NC}$), the nitrogen atom is directly bonded to the alkyl group, not the carbon atom. The carbon atom is at the terminal position. Because the nitrogen is bonded to two carbon atoms (the alkyl carbon and the isocyano carbon), its reduction leads to a secondary amine.

Answer: Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.

Reason (R): The pigments of euglenoids are identical to those present in higher plants.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
121595.sol:
Assertion (A) is a correct statement as euglenoids are mixotrophic; they are photosynthetic in the presence of sunlight but behave as heterotrophs when deprived of it.

Reason (R) is also a correct statement according to NCERT, which states that the pigments of euglenoids are identical to those present in higher plants.

However, the presence of plant-like pigments explains their ability to perform photosynthesis in sunlight, not their heterotrophic behaviour in the dark. Therefore, both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
